name: Communication
description: Compare communication software for team messaging, video meetings, collaboration and remote work. Evaluate usability, integrations, reliability, security, search, administration and total cost.
longDescription: Communication software has become the connective tissue of modern organizations, enabling real-time and asynchronous interaction across teams, locations, and time zones. The global communication and collaboration market, valued at over $70 billion in 2024, encompasses a wide range of tools including team messaging platforms, video conferencing solutions, enterprise email, unified communications, internal communication tools, and customer-facing communication platforms. The shift to remote and hybrid work has fundamentally elevated communication tools from back-office utilities to essential business infrastructure. Slack revolutionized workplace communication with its channel-based messaging paradigm, creating a new category of team collaboration platforms that now includes Microsoft Teams, Google Chat, and Discord. Video conferencing, led by Zoom, became a household name during the pandemic and remains central to how distributed teams connect. The market has seen significant consolidation as major platform providers integrate messaging, video, phone, email, and collaboration features into unified offerings. Microsoft Teams, which grew from 20 million to over 300 million monthly active users during the pandemic, exemplifies the platform bundling strategy that characterizes the current market. The rise of asynchronous communication tools reflects the recognition that real-time communication doesn't scale across time zones and that deep work requires protected focus time. Internal communication platforms are emerging as dedicated solutions for employee engagement, digital signage, and company-wide announcements. The communication technology stack is increasingly AI-powered, with features like real-time transcription and translation, meeting summarization, smart replies, and automated scheduling becoming standard offerings. The challenges of communication tool sprawl, notification overload, and the blurring of work-life boundaries have created demand for tools that help manage attention rather than demand it.
marketOverview: The global unified communications and collaboration market was valued at $62.3 billion in 2023 and is projected to reach $112.5 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 8.2%. Microsoft Teams dominates team collaboration with over 300 million monthly active users. Slack, now part of Salesforce, has 40+ million daily active users. Zoom, which grew revenue from $330 million in 2019 to $4.5 billion in 2023, serves over 300 million daily meeting participants. The enterprise email market, dominated by Microsoft Exchange/Outlook (60% market share) and Google Gmail (30%), represents approximately $15 billion annually. The video conferencing hardware market including camera systems, speakerphones, and room kits is valued at $5.2 billion. Internal communication platforms like Workplace from Meta and Microsoft Viva represent a growing $2.5 billion segment. The contact center as a service market, converging with unified communications, is valued at $8.5 billion and growing at 16% CAGR. The Asia-Pacific region is the fastest-growing communication software market at 10.8% CAGR. AI-powered communication features including real-time translation and meeting transcription are expected to be adopted by 80% of enterprise communication platforms by 2026. The average worker uses 3.6 different communication tools daily, creating significant context-switching overhead.
buyerConsiderations: Choose the communication modes your team actually needs: messaging, voice, video, screen sharing and asynchronous updates
Test reliability and call quality across the devices and network conditions your team uses
Check integrations with calendars, project management, documents, CRM, email and other daily workflows
Evaluate search and knowledge retrieval so teams can find messages, files and decisions later
Review notification, status and focus controls that help reduce interruptions and communication overload
Validate security, access controls, retention, compliance and administration requirements
Compare mobile and desktop experiences for distributed and hybrid teams
Model total cost across users, hosts, add-ons, phone features, storage and required integrations
commonMistakes: Adopting multiple overlapping communication tools that fragment conversations across platforms, forcing team members to check several tools to find information and stay connected with different groups

Over-relying on real-time communication and instant notifications, creating constant interruptions that fragment focus time and reduce individual productivity despite increasing apparent responsiveness
Implementing communication tools without establishing usage norms and channel structure, leading to chaotic, disorganized communication where important information is lost in noisy channels

Choosing enterprise communication platforms based on consumer familiarity rather than organizational needs, selecting tools optimized for personal use that lack the security, compliance, and administration features businesses require

Neglecting to integrate communication with business workflows, keeping communication siloed from the work systems it should be connected to and losing valuable context that flows through conversations
Failing to manage the communication technology stack holistically, allowing each department to adopt different tools that create barriers to cross-functional communication and collaboration

decisionFactors.description: Evaluate messaging, audio, video, screen sharing and reliability against the team's real communication patterns.
The platform should connect naturally with the productivity, project, CRM and calendar tools the team already uses.
Simple onboarding, consistent cross-device experiences and intuitive workflows improve adoption across the organization.
Review identity management, access controls, retention, auditability and compliance capabilities before rollout.
Strong search across conversations and shared files helps turn communication into reusable organizational knowledge.
Compare user or host pricing, add-ons, usage limits and administration costs at your expected team size.

buyerJourney.awareness: Organizations typically begin evaluating new communication platforms when they face specific challenges: internal communication across a growing or distributed team becomes fragmented across email and chat tools, the organization is adopting new ways of working like hybrid or remote, or the current platform lacks features needed for scale. The COVID-19 pandemic triggered the largest-scale communication platform evaluation in history, with organizations rapidly adopting tools to support remote work. Initial discovery often comes through employee recommendations from previous roles, technology industry news, or partnership with another platform they already use (Teams with Office 365, Slack with Salesforce). Free trials and freemium versions are heavily used for initial evaluation, with many organizations starting with free versions before committing to paid plans.
buyerJourney.consideration: During evaluation, organizations typically run 2-3 platforms in parallel for 2-4 weeks, involving a cross-section of teams in the trial. Key evaluation activities include testing call and video quality in various network conditions, assessing the integration setup with existing tools, evaluating the mobile experience, and testing administrative controls. IT teams assess deployment complexity, integration with identity management, and security compliance. Department heads evaluate whether the platform improves cross-team communication and reduces email volume. Reference calls with IT leaders at similar organizations validate vendor capabilities and support quality. The evaluation often involves a pilot with a specific department or use case before broader rollout decisions are made.
buyerJourney.decision: The final decision typically involves IT leadership, department heads, and executive sponsors. Organizations that already use Microsoft 365 often choose Microsoft Teams for integration and cost efficiency. Organizations prioritizing developer-friendly integrations and channel-based communication often choose Slack. Video-first organizations may choose Zoom for its superior meeting experience. The decision considers total cost of ownership including licensing, deployment, training, and ongoing administration. Implementation typically involves a phased rollout with communication and training plans, establishing channel naming conventions and usage guidelines, integrating with key business systems, and providing support resources. Success is measured by adoption rates, reduction in internal email volume, improvements in cross-team communication, and employee satisfaction with communication tools.

pricingOverview: Communication software ranges from free plans to enterprise contracts. Compare the actual cost of users or hosts, meeting and phone features, storage, administration, integrations and usage limits. Bundled suites can also change the economics when your organization already pays for Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace.

bestFor.smb: Choose a simple messaging and meeting platform that your team will adopt consistently, with enough integrations for everyday workflows.
bestFor.enterprise: Prioritize governance, identity management, compliance, administration, reliability and deep integration with the existing enterprise stack.
bestFor.free: Use a capable free tier for smaller teams when its message history, meeting limits, integrations and administration controls meet your needs.

faqs.question: Should I choose Microsoft Teams, Slack or Zoom?
faqs.answer: Choose based on your existing stack and primary workflow. Teams is especially compelling for Microsoft 365 organizations, Slack for channel-based collaboration and integrations, and Zoom when video meetings are the main priority.

faqs.question: What should I look for in communication software?
faqs.answer: Prioritize the communication modes you need, reliability, integrations, search, security, administration, usability and total cost at your expected team size.

faqs.question: How can I reduce communication tool overload?
faqs.answer: Standardize which tool is used for messaging, meetings, project work and formal communication. Reduce overlapping platforms and establish notification and response-time norms.

faqs.question: Is asynchronous communication important for remote teams?
faqs.answer: Yes. Asynchronous updates can reduce unnecessary meetings and support teams across time zones. Look for searchable messages, documented decisions and clear workflows for when real-time communication is necessary.

faqs.question: How much does business communication software cost?
faqs.answer: Costs vary by users, hosts, features, meeting limits, phone services, storage and add-ons. Compare the full monthly or annual cost for your actual team rather than a headline starting price.
